task.description: Independently re-verify ELIXIR-DEV's REQ-232 claims: parity-phrasing retirement, divergence-line preservation, .zig citation count, comment-only scope, and factual accuracy of rewritten technical claims.

verification.divergence_lines: re-ran grep: 2 lines present (metrics_exposition.ex:67, promotions.ex:410). Diffed each against main via git show -- content is byte-identical; only promotions.ex's line number shifted (409->410) due to an earlier unrelated line insertion in the same file. Confirmed genuine preservation, not just presence.
verification.zig_citation_sum: re-ran grep -c '.zig' across all 16 router files, summed manually: 88 == 88. Confirmed.
verification.scope: git diff --stat main...feature/WF02-REQ232-20260905 touches exactly the 12 named router files plus the two handoff JSONs under handoffs/WF02-REQ232-20260905/. No requirements.yaml or anti-patterns.md touched. No scope creep.
verification.diff_content_check: Read the full diff (500 lines) end to end. Every changed line falls inside a moduledoc heredoc or a `#` comment block -- no function body, @spec, route macro, or pattern match was altered. Confirmed comment/moduledoc-only.
spot_checks: instances.ex route-ordering: verified actual declarations -- rebind-pins/cancel/reconstruct all appear before any bare post "/:id" (none exists in this module). Plug.Router first-match-wins is the accurate mechanism cited.

definitions.ex DELETE handler: read handle_delete/2 -- it is a get_by_id/2 call followed by a case dispatch on status, genuinely non-atomic (two separate calls to Definitions functions), confirming 'an existing race in the underlying status model, not one this router introduces' is accurate, not invented.

tenants.ex deactivation gate: read lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex directly -- the deactivation check runs unconditionally for all HTTP methods including GET/HEAD (moduledoc @1: 'Runs for every HTTP method'), confirming the rewritten sentence's claim that gating only writes would leave a readable hole is accurate to the real implementation.
audit.ex 422 check: confirmed the from>to check happens in the router before any store query, matching the rewritten route-boundary-validation claim.
tasks.ex claim-policy-key rewrite: confirmed against the router's own policy table -- claim uses :TasksComplete, consistent with the claimed 'completion-track action, not assignment' framing.

gate_checks.type_safety_gaps: None found -- no transition logic touched.
gate_checks.scope_creep: None -- change is exactly the requested 12-file comment retirement, no framework/abstraction added.

result.not_independently_rerun: mix compile/mix test were not re-run in this session -- no Elixir/mix toolchain available in this environment (command not found). All content-level claims (grep counts, diff scope, byte-identical divergence lines, code-level accuracy of 5 spot-checked rewritten sentences) were independently re-derived directly; only the compile/test command outputs are taken from ELIXIR-DEV's report, consistent with this being a comment-only change with no code path altered.

test_designer_call.reasoning: This is a pure comment/moduledoc text change -- confirmed above that no function body, @spec, route macro, or pattern match was touched in any of the 12 files. No new behavior, no new branch, no new error path was introduced for a test to cover; the existing test suite (which already covers all router behavior) is unaffected by construction, not merely by report. Per ISS-0469's precedent (REVIEWER skip call for an equivalent no-new-behavior change), routing directly to ORCH for Step Final rather than TEST-DESIGNER.
